headline: How long does it take to find a soulmate the second time?

voc.why: Shared how-long pull; counts not recorded.

note:
Soulmate age-band batch (2026-08-19), 55-64 HOW-LONG rung.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴🔴 NO DURATION — see cards-keeps-waiting for the full argument. The headline asks for a LENGTH and a length is not a date, so the standing date ban does not catch it. Banned: any span, any pace, any 'second time is quicker', any comparison of the two in time.

🔴 NEVER PRESUME HOW THE FIRST ONE ENDED — divorce or death, the read must hold for both. No 'your divorce', no 'since he passed', no 'your ex', NO MEDIUMSHIP. 🔴 No ruling on the first man and no blame on her for it.

The word doing the work is SECOND: she is counting, and the count is what hurts. Her fear is that the first used up her chance and she is starting from behind. The finding that answers it: she is not behind. She came back carrying what the first one taught her, and that weight is why this one feels slower — not because she is late.

🔴 No promised arrival, no PLACE, no self-blame, no strategy.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — the lilies at the front have long stems and stand straight.
You asked how long it takes to find a soulmate the second time. Your hand went to the man who begins.
So there's no rule for a second one, dear. I won't pretend there is.
And that table is set the same as it ever was, dear. Nothing missing.
But you come to it knowing things now, dear. You didn't before.
That's why this one feels heavier, dear. You're carrying what the first one taught you.
Let me look closer at what came with you from the first…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — a small mark sits in the bottom corner of the card.
You asked how long it takes to find a soulmate the second time. Your hand went to the card that holds still.
So no clock runs on this card, dear. Not the first time, and not now.
And this card keeps no score, dear. First or second, it reads the same.
But you've been keeping score yourself, dear. First, second, and how far behind.
That's why this feels like catching up, dear. You've been counting from where you started over.
Let me look closer at what has been running that count…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the cliff below him is layered like steps of rock.
You asked how long it takes to find a soulmate the second time. Your hand went to the one who sets out.
So I can't time it for you, dear. Nobody walks this at a set pace.
And that card has no second time on it, dear. Every step out is a first.
But you've walked out before, dear. You know what the ground does.
That's why you're slower now, dear. You're watching where you put your foot.
Let me look closer at what has made the ground feel unsafe…
